market_name: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO by December 31, 2026?

predictions.asset: European natural gas / energy risk premium

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market move is corroborated by any Reuters/AP headline or is pure Polymarket drift; watch TTF and UNG tape for confirmation.
time_plan.1h: Reassess if European gas futures are moving in the same direction; if not, treat as noise.
time_plan.2h: Look for official Ukrainian or US statements; gauge whether a broader peace framework is implied vs. an isolated NATO clause.
time_plan.6h: Evaluate follow-through in energy and whether risk premium compression is holding or fading.
time_plan.12h: Mark final move vs. expectation; note whether the signal preceded public reporting (leak test).

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the probability that Ukraine pledges not to join NATO — a central Russian precondition — would read as de-escalation progress toward a settlement, easing the war-risk premium embedded in European (and by correlation global) gas. UNG is an imperfect US-centric proxy; the cleaner exposure is European TTF, which historically swings 5-15% on Ukraine war headlines. A credible NATO-renunciation step could compress the geopolitical premium.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether the probability jump is real news-driven; check Rheinmetall/European defense pre-market if available.
time_plan.1h: Compare ITA vs. European defense names — European should lead if thesis holds.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether commentary frames this as genuine peace progress or a symbolic clause with no ceasefire.
time_plan.6h: Check durability; peace headlines often reverse, re-inflating defense.
time_plan.12h: Record final move and whether US proxy showed any reaction at all.

predictions.reasoning: A Ukraine NATO-renunciation pledge signals movement toward a negotiated settlement, which at the margin reduces expectations of sustained elevated European defense spending. European pure-plays (Rheinmetall) are most sensitive; ITA is a weakly-exposed US proxy whose order book is dominated by US procurement, so the move is likely small and noisy. Included at low confidence because the mapping is real but diluted.

evidence_used: Market question: Ukraine pledging not to join NATO, a known core Russian demand in any settlement
Historical sensitivity of European natural gas (TTF) to Russia-Ukraine de-escalation/escalation news
Defense equities' (esp. Rheinmetall and European primes) documented reaction to war-trajectory headlines
Resolution criteria allow partial/preliminary agreements, raising odds a move reflects early peace-process signaling
uncertainty_notes: A NATO clause is only one component of a settlement; markets may not react until a ceasefire/territorial deal is credible.
Polymarket probability moves can be driven by liquidity/noise rather than genuine information.
US-listed proxies (UNG, ITA) are weakly exposed vs. European TTF and Rheinmetall, muting the signal.
700bps threshold is unlikely to be met by these diversified ETFs in 12h; cleaner exposure is non-US instruments.

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability that Ukraine agrees not to join NATO would be read as incremental progress toward a negotiated end to the war, easing the geopolitical risk premium. The cleanest public-market implications are lower European energy (gas) risk premium and modestly weaker defense equities. US-listed proxies (UNG, ITA) capture this only weakly, so expected moves are below the tradable threshold and confidence is low; the sharper, more direct instruments are European TTF gas and European defense primes like Rheinmetall.
key_assumptions: The probability move reflects genuine information about peace-process progress, not noise.
A NATO-renunciation pledge is interpreted as de-escalatory rather than as capitulation prolonging conflict.
Energy and defense remain the most war-sensitive liquid sectors.
failure_modes: The pledge is symbolic/isolated with no ceasefire, so assets barely move.
News is already public and priced, leaving no edge.
Chosen US ETFs are too diversified/weakly exposed to register a 700bps move.
Move reverses as peace optimism fades or Russia rejects other terms.
A NATO clause could paradoxically signal escalation if framed as a forced concession, inverting the reaction.
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
